anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have both their isolated-side ground pins (GND2, pin 5) connected to the same global GND net as their primary-side ground pins (GND1, pin 4).
anomalies.expected: The specification describes two isolated CAN buses implemented through isolated CAN transceivers. For a galvanically isolated CAN transceiver, GND1 and GND2 must be separate ground domains; tying GND2 to the main GND defeats the isolation.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The CAN buses are not galvanically isolated from the CM4/robot ground as intended, removing the intended noise/ground-loop isolation and potentially exposing the compute side to motor-side ground disturbances.

anomalies.observed: C42 is listed with value "22pF 100v", but its own description and MPN identify it as a 22 nF capacitor, and the three corresponding center-tap capacitors C44, C45, and C46 are all "22nF 100v".
anomalies.expected: For this Ethernet transformer/common-mode network, the four center-tap capacitors should match; the component metadata and the identical parts C44-C46 indicate C42 should be 22 nF, not 22 pF.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "C42") (value "22pF 100v") ... (description " 100V 22nF X7R ±10% 0603 Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors MLCC - SMD/SMT ROHS ") ... (field (name "MPN") "CC0603KRX7R0BB223"))

anomalies.impact: A 22 pF capacitor instead of 22 nF on one transformer center tap unbalances the Ethernet common-mode/center-tap filtering, which can degrade Ethernet signal integrity and EMI performance.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows two likely deviations from the intended design: the isolated CAN transceiver secondary grounds are tied to the main GND, defeating the specified CAN isolation, and C42 is labeled 22 pF while its metadata and matching circuit parts indicate it should be 22 nF.
